entries.name: Currency: Belly
entries.text:
Belly is the primary monetary unit established by the World Government and accepted across most of the seas. While it is the standard currency, other valuables such as gold, gems, rare weapons, or Devil Fruits can also serve as trade goods, either bartered directly or exchanged for Belly based on their assessed value.
Although most islands recognize Belly, certain isolated nations mint and use their own forms of coinage. Merchants are often willing to exchange between currencies, though rates may vary depending on distance from the Grand Line and local economy.

sections.name: Denominations
sections.text:
Belly exists in both coin and paper form:
Coins. ฿1, ฿5, ฿10, ฿50, ฿100, ฿500
Paper Notes. ฿1,000, ฿5,000, ฿10,000
There are no fractional units, though individual islands may produce additional denominations at the DM’s discretion.

sections.name: Conversion Rates
sections.text: To align Belly with traditional D&D currency, use the following approximate rates:

sections.name: Alternate Currencies
sections.text:
Some regions maintain unique currencies, reflecting their culture and distance from the World Government.
Extol (Skypiea). A currency used on the Sky Islands. Exchange rate is 10,000 Extol = 1 ฿.
Gor (Amazon Lily). Currency of the Kuja tribe.
Suggested rate is 100 Gor = 1 ฿.
Wano Coinage. Silver, gold, and platinum coins used in Wano Kuni align with the above D&D conversion table.

entries.name: Expenses
entries.text: Sometimes long journeys across the ocean allow for some extended periods of downtime while occasionally stopping by various islands to gather supplies. Even stepping away from the dangerous life of pirating for a while and spending time in a small village or large city isn’t all that uncommon for those looking for a short break from the unforgiving seas. However, living comfortably in any situation can cost quite a bit of money. Depending on a character’s lifestyle and career, these expenses will begin to stack up over time.

sections.name: Lifestyle expenses
sections.text: A character’s lifestyle represents their standard of living during downtime. Some pirates scrape by on stale bread and seawater, while others lounge in mansions, dine on banquets, and wear silks. The table below lists the daily costs associated with each tier.

sections.name: Wretched Lifestyle
sections.text: You live in squalor, scavenging or stealing for food. Your gear is neglected and your appearance shows clear signs of poverty and malnutrition.

sections.name: Poor Lifestyle
sections.text: You scrape by with the bare necessities—cheap food, water, and a small shelter. Your equipment is poorly maintained, and you rarely look clean.

sections.name: Comfortable Lifestyle
sections.text: You live modestly, affording a decent home or room aboard a ship. You eat average meals, maintain your gear, and keep a clean, acceptable appearance.

sections.name: Wealthy Lifestyle
sections.text: You enjoy fine living: a large home, spacious ship cabin, or quality inn. Your equipment is well-kept, and your appearance reflects higher social standing.

sections.name: Rich Lifestyle
sections.text: You live in luxury, with mansions, lavish cabins, or ownership of inns. Your gear is pristine, your clothes fine, and your presence commands respect.

sections.name: Noble Lifestyle
sections.text: You stand among the elite of this world. Wealth grants you the best homes, ships, clothes, and weapons, all in flawless condition.

sections.name: Food and Drink
sections.text: Meals are already included in lifestyle costs, but characters may purchase individual food and drink separately.

sections.name: Services
sections.text: Cities and ports offer more than goods, they provide services that even pirates and adventurers must rely upon. From medical attention to hiring professionals, the following costs serve as a baseline.

entries.name: Armor and Shields
entries.text:
Technology in the One Piece world varies greatly across islands, with some of the finest armor found in Marine stores or rare markets along the Grand Line. Pirates and marines often favor gear that balances comfort, mobility, and durability for seafaring life, as heavy metal armor corrodes quickly in saltwater and hinders movement aboard ships.
The Armor table provides cost, weight, and properties of the most common armors.
Armor Proficiency. Anyone can wear armor or wield a shield, but only the proficient use them effectively. Without proficiency, you suffer disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and attack rolls, and cannot cast spells.
Stealth. Armor that lists “Disadvantage” in the Stealth column imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Shields. A wooden or metal shield occupies one hand and grants a +2 bonus to AC. Only one shield can be used at a time.

sections.name: Light Armor
sections.text:
Light armor favors speed and agility while offering basic protection. Wearers add their full Dexterity modifier to AC.
Dense Coat. Durable fabrics that offer simple, practical defense.
Thick Shirt. Heavier cloth or leather that resists blows without restricting movement.
Light Bulletproof Shirt. A fiber-lined undershirt designed to stop bullets and blades.

sections.name: Medium Armor
sections.text: Medium armor strengthens defenses with tougher materials but limits agility. Wearers add their Dexterity modifier to AC, up to a maximum of +2.

sections.name: Armor Information
sections.text:
Hide. Heavy furs and pelts, common among tribes and beasts.
Bulletproof Jacket. A reinforced jacket offering strong ballistic protection with mobility.
Scale Mail. Leather with overlapping metal scales, resembling fish armor.
Bulletproof Suit. A reinforced suit protecting vital organs while leaving limbs lighter.
Sea King Half Plate. Forged from Sea King hide and scales, providing immense durability.

sections.name: Heavy Armor
sections.text:
Heavy armor is the strongest protection, worn by juggernauts with the strength to endure its bulk. Wearers do not add Dexterity modifiers to AC, but negative modifiers do not penalize them either.
Ring Mail. Leather reinforced with metal rings, cheap but serviceable.
Chain Mail. Interlocking metal rings over padded cloth; a balanced defense.
Splint. Metal strips riveted to leather, with chain at the joints for flexibility.
Steel Wootz Armor. Full plate of interlocking steel, complete with gauntlets, boots, and layered padding. Sometimes gilded for display.

sections.name: Donning and Doffing Armor
sections.text: Putting on or removing armor takes time depending on its category. You gain the armor’s AC bonus only after the full donning time is completed. If another creature assists you, doffing time is halved.

entries.name: Weapons
entries.text:
Weapons define a fighter as much as their skill. Whether it’s a cutlass, pistol, or improvised club, the weapon you wield, and your ability to wield it well, often decides life or death on the seas.
The Weapons table lists the most common arms found across the One Piece world, including their cost, weight, damage, and special properties.

sections.name: Weapon Proficiency
sections.text: Classes, races, and feats grant proficiency with specific weapon groups, classified as simple or martial. If you are proficiency with a weapon, add your proficiency bonus to attack rolls.

sections.name: Improvised Weapons
sections.text:
Any object can become a weapon in desperate hands.
Damage. Improvised weapons deal 1d4 damage (type determined by the DM).
Thrown. Range of 20 ft. (normal) / 60 ft. (long).
Proficiency. If the item is similar to a known weapon (e.g., chair leg as a club), the DM may allow proficiency to apply.

sections.name: Special Weapons
sections.text:
Some weapons function differently than others:
Lance. Disadvantage on attacks against targets within 5 ft. Requires two hands unless mounted.
Net. On a hit, restrains a Large or smaller creature until freed. A creature can escape with a DC 10 Strength check, or by

sections.name: Simple Weapons
sections.text: destroying the net (AC 10, 5 slashing damage). Attacks made with a net are limited to one per action, bonus action, or reaction.

sections.name: Weapon Properties
sections.text:
Weapons may have one or more properties that alter how they function, such as finesse, heavy, light, loading, range, reach, special, thrown, two-handed, or versatile. These properties function as described in the standard 5e rules.
In addition, there are additional properties not found in 5e rules.
Concealed. You have advantage on Dexterity or Intelligence (Sleight of Hand) checks made to conceal this weapon on your person.
Concussing. Once per turn when you hit a creature concentrating with a concussing weapon, the creature subtracts your proficiency bonus from its concentration saves.
Defensive. While wielding a defensive weapon, the weapon gives a +1 to AC.
Finisher. When you damage a prone creature with a finisher weapon, you roll an additional weapon damage die.
Push. If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature 5 feet away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
Ricochet. The weapon returns to your hand after a hit or miss provided you have a free hand.
Fist. This weapon cannot attack normally. Instead, the weapons damage is added onto your unarmed damage when equipped.

entries.name: Adventuring Gear
entries.text: This section describes items that have special rules or require further explanation.

sections.name: Adventuring Items
sections.text:
Acid. As an action, you can splash the contents of this vial onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the acid as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 acid damage.
Antitoxin. A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. It confers no benefit to undead or constructs.
Ball Bearings. As an action, you can spill these tiny metal balls from their pouch to cover a level area 10 feet square. A creature moving across the covered area must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn’t need to make the saving throw.
Block and Tackle. A set of pulleys with a cable threaded through them and a hook to attach to objects, a block and tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.
Book. A book might contain poetry, historical accounts, information pertaining to a particular field of lore, diagrams and notes on dial contraptions, or just about anything else that can be represented using text or pictures.
Caltrops. As an action, you can spread a single bag of caltrops to cover a 5-foot-square area. Any creature that enters the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or stop moving and take 1 piercing damage. Until the creature regains at least 1 hit point, its walking speed is reduced by 10 feet. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn’t need to make the saving throw.
Candle. For 1 hour, a candle sheds bright light in a 5- foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.
Case, Gun Bullets. This wooden case can hold up to twenty gun bullets or five bazooka rounds.
Case, Map or Scroll. This cylindrical leather case can hold up to ten rolled-up sheets of paper or five rolled-up sheets of parchment.
Chain. A chain has 10 hit points. It can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength check
Climber’s Kit. A climber’s kit includes special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. You can use the climber’s kit as an action to anchor yourself; when you do, you can’t fall more than 25 feet from the point where you anchored yourself, and you can’t climb more than 25 feet away from that point without undoing the anchor.
Component Pouch. A component pouch is a small, watertight leather belt pouch that has compartments to hold all the material components and other special items you need to cast your spells, except for those components that have a specific cost (as indicated in a spell’s description).
Crowbar. Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crow bar’s leverage can be applied.
Fire Explosive. Explosives require a method of being lit using heat or fire, and then being thrown. As an action, you can throw this explosive up to 20 feet, letting it explode where it lands. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the explosive as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns. If it hits a flammable material or object, it will begin to burn away a random 5-foot cube of the material each round. A creature can end this damage or fire spread by using its action to make a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames or toss water on it.
Fishing Tackle. This kit includes a wooden rod, silken line, corkwood bobbers, steel hooks, lead sinkers, velvet lures, and narrow netting.
Handcuffs These metal restraints can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the handcuffs requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of m anacles com es with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves’ tools can pick the handcuffs’ lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Handcuffs have 15 hit points.
Healer’s Kit. This kit is a leather pouch containing bandages, salves, and splints. The kit has ten uses. As an action, you can expend one use of the kit to stabilize a creature that has 0 hit points, without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.
Holy Symbol. A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. A Priest can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus, as described in chapter 10 of the D&D 5th Edition Player’s Handbook. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.
Holy Water. As an action, you can splash the contents of this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a target creature, treating the holy water as an improvised weapon. If the target is a fiend or undead, it takes 2d6 radiant damage.
A priest may create holy water by performing a special ritual. The ritual takes 1 hour to perform, uses ฿250,000 worth of powdered silver and special salts, and requires the caster to expend a 1st-level spell slot.
Hunting Trap. When you use your action to set it, this trap form s a saw-toothed steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and stop moving. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet long). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 piercing damage to the trapped creature.
Lamp. A lamp casts bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.
Lantern, Bullseye. A bullseye lantern casts bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.
Lantern, Hooded. A hooded lantern casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil. As an action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.
Lock. A key is provided with the lock. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves’ tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Your DM may decide that better locks are available for higher prices.
Log Pose. A log pose, similar to a compass, helps navigators find their way to nearby islands or locations. However, log poses are special in that they are the only way to navigate on the Grand Line, since regular compasses don’t work there. A log pose is used by spending a certain amount of time on an island (which could take hours, days, or years) to record the magnetic waves required to point it toward the next nearby island. Paradise log poses do not work in the New World, so a New World log pose is required to navigate there. New World log poses are 10 times more expensive than an ordinary log pose.
Mess Kit. This tin box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl.
Oil. Oil usually comes in a clay flask that holds 1 pint. As an action, you can splash the oil in this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a target creature or object, treating the oil as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target is covered in oil. If the target takes any fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an additional 5 fire damage from the burning oil. You can also pour a flask of oil on the ground to cover a 5-foot-square area, provided that the surface is level. If lit, the oil burns for 2 rounds and deals 5 fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn in the area. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
Poison, Basic. You can use the poison in this vial to coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. Applying the poison takes an action. A creature hit by the poisoned weapon or ammunition must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 1d4 poison damage. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.
Pouch. A cloth or leather pouch can hold up to 20 sling bullets or 50 blowgun needles, among other things. A compartmentalized pouch for holding spell components is called a component pouch (described earlier in this section).
Power Source. A power source is a special item—a battery, a special dial, an energy crystal, a fuel rod, or a similar item—designed to channel the power of abilities and spells. A tinkerer can use such an item as a spellcasting focus, as described in chapter 10 of the 5th Edition D&D Players Handbook.
Quiver. A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.
Ram, Portable. You can use a portable ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check.
Rations. Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.
Rope. Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.
Scale, Merchant’s. A scale includes a small balance, pans, and a suitable assortment of weights up to 2 pounds. With it, you can measure the exact weight of small objects, such as raw precious metals or trade goods, to help determine their worth.
Spyglass. Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.
Tent. A simple and portable canvas shelter, a tent sleeps two.
Tinderbox. This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch—or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel—takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.
Torch. A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

sections.name: Equipment Packs
sections.text:
The starting equipment you get from your class includes a collection of useful adventuring gear, put together in a pack. The contents of these packs are listed here. If you are buying your starting equipment, you can purchase a pack for the price shown, which might be cheaper than buying the items individually.
Burglar’s Pack (฿160,000). Includes a backpack, a bag of 1,000 ball bearings, 10 feet of string, a bell, 5 candles, a crowbar, a hammer, 10 pitons, a hooded lantern, 2 flasks of oil, 5 days rations, a tinderbox, and a waterskin. The pack also has 50 feet of hempen rope strapped to the side of it.
Diplomat’s Pack (฿390,000). Includes a chest, 2 cases for maps and scrolls, a set of fine clothes, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, a lamp, 2 flasks of oil, 5 sheets of paper, a vial of perfume, sealing wax, and soap.
Dungeoneer’s Pack (฿120,000). Includes a backpack, a crowbar, a hammer, 10 pitons, 10 torches, a tinderbox, 10 days of rations, and a waterskin. The pack also has 50 feet of hempen rope strapped to the side of it.
Entertainer’s Pack (฿400,000). Includes a backpack, a bedroll, 2 costumes, 5 candles, 5 days of rations, a waterskin, and a disguise kit.
Explorer’s Pack (฿100,000). Includes a backpack, a bedroll, a mess kit, a tinderbox, 10 torches, 10 days of rations, and a waterskin. The pack also has 50 feet of hempen rope strapped to the side of it.
Pirate’s Pack (฿320,000). Includes a chest, 2 cases for maps and scrolls, a set of traveler’s clothes, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, a lamp, 2 flasks of oil, 5 sheets of paper, a tankard, 20 days of rations, fishing tackle, soap, a hammer, and a small knife. The pack also has 50 feet of hempen rope strapped to the side of it.
Priest’s Pack (฿190,000). Includes a backpack, a blanket, 10 candles, a tinderbox, an alms box, 2 blocks of incense, a censer, vestments, 2 days of rations, and a waterskin.
Scholar’s Pack (฿400,000). Includes a backpack, a book of lore, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, 10 sheets of parchment, a little bag of sand, and a small knife.

sections.name: Tools
sections.text:
Your class, race, and background will give you proficiency with tools. Tools are designed to assist you in performing a certain task such as repairing, building, playing music, or any other similar activity. When you are proficient with a certain type of tool, you add your proficiency bonus to checks made when using that particular tool. Tool checks can use a number of different abilities, not just one.
For the most part, these tools operate the same as they do in D&D 5th Edition, with a few exceptions.

sections.name: Tools
sections.text:
Artisan’s Tools. These special tools include the items needed to pursue a craft or trade. The Tools table shows examples of the most common types of tools, each providing items related to a single craft. Proficiency with a set of artisan’s tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make using the tools in your craft. Each type of artisan’s tools requires a separate proficiency.
Disguise Kit. This pouch of cosmetics, hair dye, and small props lets you create disguises that change your physical appearance. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a visual disguise.
Forgery Kit. This small box contains a variety of papers and parchments, pens and inks, seals and sealing wax, gold and silver leaf, and other supplies necessary to create convincing forgeries of physical documents. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a physical forgery of a document.
Gaming Set. This item encompasses a wide range of game pieces, including dice and decks of cards (for games such as Poker). A few common examples appear on the Tools table, but other kinds of gaming sets exist. If you are proficient with a gaming set, you can add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make to play a game with that set. Each type of gaming set requires a separate proficiency.
Herbalism Kit. This kit contains a variety of instruments such as clippers, mortar and pestle, and pouches and vials used by herbalists to create remedies and potions. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to identify or apply herbs. Also, proficiency with this kit is required to create antitoxin and potions of healing.
Musical Instrument. Several of the most common types of musical instruments are shown on the table as examples. If you have proficiency with a given musical instrument, you can add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to play music with the instrument. A bard can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus. Each type of musical instrument requires a separate proficiency.
Navigator’s Tools. This set of instruments is used for navigation at sea. Proficiency with navigator’s tools lets you chart a ship’s course and follow navigation charts. In addition, these tools allow you to add your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make to avoid getting lost at sea.
Poisoner’s Kit. A poisoner’s kit includes the vials, chemicals, and other equipment necessary for the creation of poisons. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to craft or use poisons.
Thieves’ Tools. This set of tools includes a small file, a set of lock picks, a small mirror mounted on a metal handle, a set of narrow-bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers. Proficiency with these tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to disarm traps or open locks.

entries.name: Den Den Mushi
entries.text:
Den Den Mushi are a species of telepathic snails used across the seas for long-distance communication. When fitted with receivers, dials, or other accessories, they can transmit sound, and in some cases images, over impressive ranges. Most are customized to suit their owner’s needs, from paintjobs and fittings to technological upgrades like range extenders or encryption seals.
While the most common Den Den Mushi are used like telephones, rarer variants serve specialized roles, such as surveillance, recording, or global emergency signals.

sections.name: Standard Den Den Mushi
sections.text:
Cost: ฿1,000,000
Maximum Range: 100 miles The most common type, used much like a telephone. Sounds spoken into one are perfectly reproduced by the connected snail. Standard Den Den Mushi are reliable across islands and nearby seas, though their range is not infinite.

sections.name: Baby Den Den Mushi
sections.text:
Cost: ฿4,000,000
Maximum Range: 10 miles Miniature snails designed for concealment, often carried in clothing or pockets. Their small size makes them ideal for covert communication but limits their signal strength.

sections.name: Black Den Den Mushi
sections.text:
Cost: ฿5,000,000
Maximum Range: 100 miles Espionage snails capable of intercepting nearby Den Den Mushi transmissions. They record and memorize conversations for later playback. Widely used by Marines, government agents, and spies.

sections.name: White Den Den Mushi
sections.text:
Cost: ฿5,000,000
Maximum Range: 1 mile Extremely rare countermeasure snails. They emit a telepathic field that prevents Black Den Den Mushi from eavesdropping within range. Favored by revolutionaries and covert operatives.

sections.name: Visual Den Den Mushi
sections.text:
Cost: ฿10,000,000
Maximum Range: 50 miles Adapted for sight rather than sound, these snails capture and transmit images or video. They can replay footage as photographs or project it onto screens using their flashing eyes. Often used for surveillance or journalism.

sections.name: Special Den Den Mushi
sections.text: The rarest and most powerful of the species, reserved for top officials. These snails transmit emergency commands on a global scale.

sections.name: Den Den Mushi Customization
sections.text: Den Den Mushi can be modified with accessories or enhancements, often found in markets or the underworld trade network. Prices vary depending on rarity and location.

sections.name: Den Den Paintjob
sections.text: Cost: ฿100,000 Cosmetic modification; Den Den Mushi can be painted or styled to match the owner’s appearance. Usually bought alongside the snail.

sections.name: Dialing Mechanism
sections.text:
Cost: ฿200,000
A mechanical attachment that allows a Den Den Mushi to actively place calls rather than only receive them. To connect, the user must input the target Den Den Mushi’s unique “snail number.” Without this upgrade, a Den Den Mushi can only answer incoming calls.

sections.name: Range Extender
sections.text: Cost: ฿10,000,000 Doubles the effective signal range of a Den Den Mushi.

sections.name: Loudspeaker
sections.text:
Cost: ฿1,000,000
Projects outgoing voice at high volume, audible up to 300 ft.

sections.name: Encryption Seal
sections.text:
Cost: ฿3,000,000
Creates a secure link; communications cannot be intercepted except by another sealed Den Den Mushi.

sections.name: Recording Node
sections.text: Cost: ฿1,500,000 Allows playback of past conversations up to 1 hour in length.

sections.name: Multi-Line Splitter
sections.text: Cost: ฿2,500,000 Enables one Den Den Mushi to hold and switch between up to 3 active connections instead of 1.

sections.name: Miniature Earpiece
sections.text:
Cost: ฿1,000,000
A custom receiver shaped for the user’s ear, allowing hands-free use.

entries.name: Dials & Dial Inventions
entries.text:
Dials are mysterious seashell devices native to the Sky Islands, each capable of storing and releasing specific forms of energy. They vary in size and strength with some serving everyday purposes like cooking, refrigeration, or generating wind, while others enhance weapons or unleash devastating power in combat.
Common dials are relatively easy to find along Sky Island shorelines, but rare dials which are larger shells used in warfare or advanced machinery, are far harder to acquire.

sections.name: Using a Dial
sections.text:
Each dial stores energy, whether it be elemental, kinetic, or otherwise, then releases it when the button on its shell is pressed. Their effectiveness depends on type and intended use, ranging from utility tools to destructive weaponry.
You may attach dials to your weapons or body however you deem fit.

sections.name: Dial Proficiency
sections.text: If you are proficient with Dials, you add your proficiency bonus to any ability check or attack roll made while using one.

sections.name: Finding a Simple Dial
sections.text: While exploring Sky Island shores, a character may spend 24 hours searching and roll a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to locate a simple dial. Characters proficient with Dials roll with advantage. On success, roll a d20 on the Simple Dial Table to determine which shell was found.

sections.name: Finding a Rare Dial
sections.text:
When searching Sky Island shores for Dials, characters roll on the Simple Dial Table as normal. However, there is always a slim chance of uncovering a Rare Dial instead.
By default, a roll of 20 on the d20 used for the Simple Dial Table indicates the discovery of a Rare Dial. If a Rare Dial is found, roll on the Rare Dial Table or have the DM assign one directly.
If you roll a Large Simple Dial, reroll on the Simple Dial Table and take the large version of the dial.

sections.name: Simple Dials
sections.text: Simple Dials store modest amounts of energy and produce practical or low-risk effects. They are common on Sky Islands and rarely overwhelming in power.

sections.name: Breath Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Breath Dial stores air, gases, or wind currents, releasing them later as a focused gust. This dial holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb up to a 5-foot cube of gas or wind within 5 feet of you. The last gas absorbed determines what is expelled.
Expel. As an action, by spending 1 charge release a stored cube of gas into a space within 5 feet. If the gas is harmful, that effect applies as normal. Creatures in the space must succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check or be pushed 5 feet away. Objects under 10 pounds are automatically pushed out.
Large Dial Variant. This dial holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
A Large Breath Dial can also power a standard Waver, reducing its construction cost to ฿1,000,000.

sections.name: Flavor Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Flavor Dial absorbs gases and scents, from foul odors to explosive vapors, and releases them later. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb up to a 5-foot cube of gas or scent. The last gas absorbed determines what is expelled.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a stored cube of gas into a space within 5 feet. The gas behaves as it normally would.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Freeze Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Freeze Dial absorbs cold energy from frigid sources such as ice, snow, or freezing air, then releases it to chill spaces or unleash icy bursts. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb cold energy from a 5-foot cube of material, spell, or gas at or below 0°C (32°F) within 5 feet.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release freezing energy into a 5-foot cube within 5 feet, lowering its temperature to freezing for up to 24 hours. This can preserve food, create iceboxes, or chill areas.
Cold Burst. As part of a weapon attack, spend 1 charge to release stored cold. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 cold damage.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Heat Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Heat Dial absorbs energy from extremely hot sources such as fire, magma, or burning gases, then releases it as searing heat. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb heat from a 5-foot cube of material or gas at or above 100°C (212°F) within 5 feet.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release heat into a 5-foot cube within 5 feet, raising it to burning or boiling temperatures for up to 24 hours. This can create ovens, heaters, or dangerous hazards.
Heat Burst. As part of a weapon attack, spend 1 charge to release stored heat. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 fire damage.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Lamp Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000 A Lamp Dial absorbs light from natural or artificial sources and re-emits it as steady illumination. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet for 1 hour.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Milky Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Milky Dial absorbs and releases chunks of cloud, creating floating pathways or barriers. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a solid 5-foot cube of cloud into a space within 5 feet. Each cube has AC 6 and 1 hit point. At the start of each of your turns, the cube remains in place or drifts up to 5 feet in a direction of your choice.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Thunder Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Thunder Dial absorbs electrical energy from natural or artificial sources, then channels it into devices or unleashes it as a surge of lightning. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb electrical energy from a 5-foot cube within 5 feet, such as a lightning strike, live wire, or generator.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to channel stored electricity into a nearby device, powering it for up to 24 hours. This can operate machines such as lamps, fans, or other simple mechanisms.
Lightning Burst. As part of a weapon attack, spend 1 charge to release stored energy. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 lightning damage.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Tone Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Tone Dial records and replays sounds or spoken messages. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Record. As a bonus action, by spending 1 charge, capture up to 60 seconds of audio. The last recording determines what is played back.
Playback. As an action, press the button to replay stored sound, audible up to 120 feet. Messages may be replayed, looped (up to 1 hour per day), or erased in 10- second segments.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn. Recordings may be looped indefinitely.

sections.name: Vision Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Vision Dial captures light to create still images, functioning like a camera. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Capture. As a bonus action, spend 1 charge to take a single photo. You can only store 1 picture per vision dial.
Print. As an action, press the button to print the stored photo onto paper or parchment, deleting the image from the dial.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn. By spending 2 charges, record a video up to 10 seconds long. Videos may be projected directly from the dial, and individual frames can be printed without deleting the stored file.

sections.name: Water Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Uncommon
Cost: ฿500,000
A Water Dial absorbs liquids and releases them later in controlled amounts. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb a 5-foot cube of water or liquid within 5 feet. The last absorbed liquid determines what is expelled.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release liquid into a space within 5 feet. The liquid pours naturally, filling containers, spreading across surfaces, or extinguishing flames.
Large Dial Variant. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.

sections.name: Rare Dials
sections.text: Rare Dials, by contrast, are designed for combat and capable of unleashing devastating bursts of energy. Their immense force can endanger both the wielder and their target when released.

sections.name: Axe Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 Axe Dials are among the most powerful combat dials, designed to amplify the force of physical attacks. Attaching an Axe Dial to a weapon or body part requires a short or long rest. A weapon or body part can only benefit from one dial at a time, and bonuses from multiple dials do not stack.
While an Axe Dial is attached to a weapon or body part, damage rolls made with that weapon or body part gain a bonus equal to your proficiency bonus.

sections.name: Eisen Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
An Eisen Dial absorbs and releases chunks of dense iron cloud, forming floating barriers or weapons. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Expel Iron Clouds. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a 5-foot cube of iron cloud into a space within 5 feet. Each cube has AC 20 and 30 hit points, drifting up to 5 feet at the start of your turn in a direction you choose. When destroyed, it shatters into metallic dust.
Weapon Creation. As an action, you may release a 5- foot cube of stored cloud and shape it into a simple melee weapon of your choice. If you are proficient with Dials, you are also proficient with this weapon. The weapon lasts for 1 hour or until dispelled as a bonus action, after which it crumbles into dust.

sections.name: Flame Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
A Flame Dial absorbs fire or burning material and unleashes it as scorching blasts. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb fire from a 5-foot cube of flame, magma, or burning material within 5 feet.
Expel. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a blazing ray of fire at a target within 60 feet. Make a ranged attack using any ability score of your choice for the attack roll. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 fire damage.

sections.name: Flash Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
A Flash Dial absorbs light from natural or artificial sources and unleashes it as a blinding burst. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Flash. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a burst of light. All creatures within 30 feet of the dial (except the user) must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of their next turn.

sections.name: Ball Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
A Ball Dial absorbs and releases chunks of cloud, creating static balls of cloud. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Expel Cloud Balls. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a 5-foot ball of cloud into a space within 5 feet. At the start of each round, the ball remains in place or drifts up to 5 feet in any direction of your choice at the

sections.name: Combat Ball Surge Table
sections.text:
start of your turn. Each cube has AC 6 and 1 hit point. Balls can attach to one another without breaking, forming floating chains or clusters.
Ranged Attack. A ball can be pushed up to 30 feet in any direction as a ranged weapon attack. It bursts on impact with the first creature or object it touches. You may use any ability score when making a weapon attack with this dial.
When a cloud ball is destroyed or popped, roll on one of the Ball Surge tables below. The resulting effect targets the nearest creature to the ball or the ball itself, if no creature is within 5 feet of the ball.

rows: d20 Effect 1 Static shocks erupt, dealing 1d6 lightning damage to all creatures within 5 ft. 2 A deafening bang bursts. Creatures within 10 ft. must succeed on a DC 12 Con save or be deafened for 1 minute. 3 Colored smoke fills a 10-ft. radius, heavily obscuring the area for 1 minute. 4 Sticky foam coats the nearest creature. They are restrained until the end of their next turn unless they succeed on a DC 12 Strength save. 5 Glittering sparks blind nearby creatures. All creatures within 10 ft. must succeed on a DC 12 Dex save or be blinded until the start of their next turn. 6 Freezing mist bursts forth. The nearest creature takes 1d6 cold damage and has their speed reduced by 10 ft. until the end of their next turn. 7 A concussive boom erupts. The nearest creature has disadvantage on their next attack roll.
10 A sudden downpour erupts, drenching the nearest creature and extinguishing flames within 10 ft.

13 The ball pops into harmless confetti and streamers, coating the nearest creature.
