The nearest ally has disadvantage on their next attack roll. 7 A sweet fragrance calms the nearest ally, granting 1d4 temporary hit points, but they are also poisoned until the end of their next turn. 8 A sudden ringing noise disrupts focus. The nearest ally must succeed on a DC 12 Con save or lose their reaction until the start of their next turn. 9 A flash of clarity inspires the nearest ally, allowing them to reroll one ability check made within the next minute.
10 A rainbow burst fills the air. All allies within 10 ft. gain advantage on their next attack roll, but enemies in the same radius do as well.

sections.name: Impact Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
An Impact Dial absorbs the force of incoming attacks and unleashes it later as a shock wave. Holds 5 charges and can store up to 30 force damage at a time. Regains 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn. Any excess damage beyond this cap cannot be absorbed and is instead taken normally.
Absorb Blow. As a reaction when targeted by an attack, spell, or damaging effect, you may expend charges to reduce the damage. For each charge spent, roll 1d10 and subtract the total from the damage taken, storing the reduced amount in the dial. You cannot store more than the total damage of the effect. If the damage is reduced to 0, the attack is completely nullified.
Expel Blow. Make a melee attack with the dial, expending stored force. On a hit, the target takes additional force damage equal to the amount released. Regardless of the result, the user takes half of the expended force damage (rounded down) as recoil.

sections.name: Jet Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 A Jet Dial absorbs powerful gusts of wind and releases them in concentrated bursts, propelling the user or machinery at high speeds. Holds 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Absorb. As a bonus action, absorb a 5-foot cube of strong wind or gas within 5 feet. The last absorbed source determines the expelled force.
Expel. As a bonus action, spend 1 charge to propel yourself 30 feet in any direction.
Waver Integration. Attaching a Jet Dial to a Waver doubles its travel speed.

sections.name: Reject Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 The Reject Dial is one of the rarest and most dangerous dials in existence. Absorbing the force of incoming attacks and unleashes it later as a devastating shock wave. However, its immense recoil makes it incredibly risky to use, often being as lethal to the wielder as to their target. Holds 10 charges and can store up to 60 force damage at a time. Regains 1d6 + 4 charges each dawn.
Absorb Blow. As a reaction when targeted by an attack, spell, or damaging effect, you may expend charges to reduce the damage. For each charge spent, roll 1d20 and subtract the total from the damage taken, storing the reduced amount in the dial. You cannot store more than the total damage of the effect. If the damage is reduced to 0, the attack is completely nullified.
Expel Shock Wave. Release stored force in a melee attack. On a hit, the target takes additional force damage equal to the expended amount, and the user suffers recoil damage equal to half the expended total (rounded down).

sections.name: Storm Dial
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (dial), Rare (requires proficiency with dials to use)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 A Storm Dial absorbs and releases condensed storm clouds charged with violent winds and lightning. Holds 5 charges, regaining 1d4 + 1 charges each dawn.
Expel Lightning Cloud. As an action, spend 1 charge to release a 5-foot cube of storm cloud into a space within 5 feet. Each cube lasts 1 minute or until it has made attacks for 3 rounds.
At the start of each round, each cloud automatically targets the nearest creature within 30 feet, dealing 1d6 lightning damage.
Any creature that ends its turn inside a storm cloud must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage from crushing winds.

sections.name: Dial Inventions
sections.text: Dial Weapons are conventional arms enhanced with the shell technology of Skypiea and other Sky Islands. These unique devices store elemental forces, energy, or sound, releasing them in powerful bursts when activated.

sections.name: Burn Blade
sections.text:
Weapon (scimitar), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
This simple wooden hilt contains a rare Breath Dial that projects a high-pressure jet of flame, forming a razor edge of fire. When active, the Burn Blade cuts through wood and scorches steel. This weapon is a magical weapon.
Flame Edge. As a bonus action, you can ignite or extinguish the Burn Blade. While active, it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet, and attacks made with it deal an additional 1d6 fire damage. The blade can remain active for up to 10 minutes per long rest.
When you hit a creature or object made of wood, plant matter, or other flammable material, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or catch fire. A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until extinguished as an action.

sections.name: Burn Bazooka
sections.text:
Weapon (bazooka), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿50,000,000
In additional to being a normal bazooka, this massive Shandian cannon channels stored thermal energy into devastating blasts of fire. The bazooka holds up to 3 charges in an internal Heat Dial Reservoir. It requires no ammunition, but expended charges replenish at each dawn.
Burn Bazooka Shot. As an action, you can expend 1 charge to fire a line of searing fire 120 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d10 fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
Overloaded Inferno. As an action, you can expend all 3 charges to release a wave of fire in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d10 fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. On a failed save, the creature also ignites, taking 1d10 fire damage at the end of each of its turns until extinguished with an action.

sections.name: Clima-Tact
sections.text:
Weapon (quarterstaff), Uncommon (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 This segmented staff, designed as a scientific marvel rather than a blade, stores “weather bubbles” that allow its wielder to bend the elements for tactical control.
While wielding the Clima-Tact, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC.
Weather Manipulation. As a bonus action, you can release a weather bubble, creating one of the following effects in a 10-foot cube within 30 feet. You can create a number of bubbles equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
Heat Bubble. Each creature in the area takes 1d4 fire damage. Creatures in the area cannot benefit from concealment caused by fog, smoke, or light cover.
Cool Bubble. Creatures that enter or start their turn there have their speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of their turn.
Thunder Bubble. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC, taking 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
Cyclone Tempo (1/Long Rest). As an action, you combine Heat and Cool bubbles into a spinning blast of wind. Creatures in a 15-foot line must make a Strength saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, they take 2d6 bludgeoning damage and are pushed 10 feet away from you. On a success, they take half damage and are not moved.

sections.name: Clima-Tact, Perfect
sections.text:
Weapon (quarterstaff), Very Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿50,000,000
This segmented staff is fitted with dial-infused spheres that amplify its weather controlling effects.
While wielding the Clima-Tact, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC.
Weather Manipulation. As a bonus action, you can release a weather bubble, creating one of the following effects in a 10-foot cube within 60 feet. You can create a number of bubbles equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
Heat Sphere. Each creature in the area takes 1d8 fire damage. Creatures in the area cannot benefit from concealment caused by fog, smoke, or light cover.
Cool Sphere. Creatures that enter or start their turn there have their speed reduced by 20 feet until the end of their turn.
Thunder Sphere. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC, taking 2d8 lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.
Thunderbolt Tempo (1/Long Rest). As an action, unleash a 30-foot line of lightning. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC, taking 3d8 lightning damage on a failed save and are pushed 10 feet away from you, or half as much and no push on a success.
Mirage Fata Morgana (1/Long Rest). Cast the mirror image spell. You create 5 illusory duplicates of yourself instead of 3.

sections.name: Eisen Whip
sections.text:
Weapon (whip), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
This segmented whip projects from an Iron Dial in its hilt, forming a flexible blade of metallic vapor. The weapon flows like smoke but strikes with the strength of steel.
When you attack with the Eisen Whip, you may choose to have it ignore half cover.
Writhing Bind. As an action, you can command the Iron Cloud to coil around a Medium or smaller creature within 10 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled until the start of your next turn.
Piercing Lance (1/Long Rest). When you successfully hit or grapple a creature with the Eisen Whip, you can cause the Iron Cloud to spear forward in a 5-foot line. The target and any creature directly behind it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 4d8 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

sections.name: Flash Gun
sections.text:
Weapon (pistol), Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
This sleek obsidian-black, dual-barreled derringer is a relic of Skypiean craftsmanship. Each shot is accompanied by a sudden flare of light, designed to confuse and disorient enemies.
When you fire the Flash Gun, it first emits a dazzling burst from its embedded Flash Dial before firing a bullet. The target and all creatures within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of their next turn. You can use this effect once per turn.
You have advantage on attack rolls with the Flash Gun against creatures blinded by its flash.

sections.name: Heat Lance
sections.text:
Weapon (lance), Uncommon (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
This long, metallic lance contains a rare Heat Dial embedded within its shaft. When activated, the tip glows red-hot, capable of both piercing and burning flesh in a single strike.
As a bonus action, you can activate the Heat Dial, causing the tip of the lance to glow red-hot. While active, the lance deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit. On a critical hit, the target ignites, taking 1d6 fire damage at the start of its turn until it or another creature uses an action to extinguish the flames.

sections.name: Jet Board
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (surfboard), Uncommon (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
Crafted from Sky Island driftwood and fitted with twin Jet Dials, this lightweight skyboard allows its rider to hover and propel themselves with bursts of compressed air.
While standing on the Jet Board, you can fly up to your walking speed, to a maximum altitude of 10 feet. If you fall off or are knocked prone, the board loses thrust and drops to the ground.
The Jet Board can support a Medium or smaller rider and up to 250 lbs. of total weight. In heavy rain or magical wind effects (such as gust of wind or control winds), you must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics or land vehicles) check to maintain control. The board loses power if submerged in water.
Jet Burst. As a bonus action, activate the Jet Dials to surge forward. Until the end of your turn, your flying speed is doubled, and you do not provoke opportunity attacks when moving. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

sections.name: Jet Skates
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (footwear), Uncommon (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
These crude but powerful skates are fitted with Jet Dials, blasting compressed air to hurl their wearer forward at reckless speeds. Your walking speed increases by 15 feet while wearing the skates. You have advantage on Acrobatics checks to maintain balance or land safely after falling up to 30 feet.
Jet Burst. As a bonus action, you can dash in a straight line up to 60 feet in any direction, gaining hover if you travel into the air. Each creature in your path must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest. You do not provoke opportunity attacks when dashing in this way.

sections.name: Ten-Fold Axe
sections.text:
Wondrous Item (battle cloth), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature proficient with dials)
Cost: ฿50,000,000
This strip of black cloth conceals ten Axe Dials sewn along one side. When unfurled, it becomes a wall of slicing force, capable of cleaving through steel and stone alike.
If you activate the Ten-Fold Axe while you are grappled, restrained, or confused, make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, you take the same slashing damage your target takes.
Slicing Surge. As an action, you may activate the dials to target a creature within 5 feet. The target must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d10 slashing damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it must also succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
Whirlbind Execution (1/Long Rest). As an action, you may unfurl the cloth in a 10-foot cone and activate all ten dials at once. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d10 slashing damage and being pushed 10 feet back on a failure, or half damage with no push on a success.

entries.name: Pop Greens
entries.text:
Pop Greens are special seeds from the forest of Greenstone on the Boin Archipelago that instantly sprout into magical plants when planted, releasing the power of a stored spell.
Pop Greens are sometimes found on remote islands or traded through the black market, where their value can reach 120% of their creation cost.

sections.name: Creating a Pop Green
sections.text:
To create a Pop Green, the crafter must have an Herbalism Kit, the appropriate materials, proficiency in Nature or Arcana, and a Pop Seed Husk. Husks act as the organic container for the magic infusion and are required for every Pop Green.
Pop Green Husks can only be imbued with spells from the Druid spell list from D&D5e. A spellcaster is not required to know or prepare the spell themselves; instead, the husk is infused with natural magic during the crafting process.

sections.name: Acquiring Husks & Husk Plants
sections.text:
Pop Seed Husks are rare, usually bought on the black market or harvested on remote tropical islands.
A Pop Seed Husk can also be planted to grow a Husk Plant, a hardy vine that produces more husks over time.
Yield. A Husk Plant produces 1d4 Pop Seed Husks per week under proper care.
Care. Each week, the planter must succeed on a DC 13 Nature or Survival check to harvest the husks. On a failed check, the plant produces nothing that week.
Environment. Husk Plants only thrive in warm or tropical climates, but may be cultivated in greenhouses with effort.

sections.name: Miracle Fertilizer
sections.text:
A planter can choose to infuse a Pop Seed Husk with special fertilizers and enriched soil during its creation. Doing so greatly accelerates the growth process, but at a steep cost.
The time and cost for creating a Pop Green depend on the level of the spell to be stored, as shown on the table below. If the stored spell is a cantrip, it functions as though cast at 1st level.

sections.name: Using a Pop Green
sections.text:
A Pop Green can be planted as an action, bonus action, or reaction (matching the stored spell’s casting time) within 5 feet, hurled up to 30 feet, or shot from a ranged weapon range into the soil. Upon planting, the seed sprouts and immediately begins casting the stored spell with no components required.
If the spell requires a target, the planter may verbally command the plant to attack specific targets.
If the spell only targets the caster, it instead affects the planter if they are within 30 feet; otherwise, it targets itself.
If the spell requires concentration, the plant attempts to maintain it until duration ends or is killed.
After the spell is completed or concentration ends, the plant instantly withers.

sections.name: Pop Green Plant Stats
sections.text:
While active, the plant is a Large plant with the following traits:
Hit Points. 5 × Spell level
Armor Class. 10 + Spell level
Vulnerability. Fire
Concentration Save. Equal to spell level
Cantrips count as 1st level spells when looking at their spell level for the plants stats.

entries.name: Stars and Special Ammo
entries.text: Special ammunition are designed to deliver additional effects beyond ordinary damage. Once fired, the projectile is destroyed, regardless of whether it hits or misses.

sections.name: Crafting Ammunition
sections.text:
Creating special ammunition requires smith’s or mason’s tools, proficiency in Arcana or Sleight of Hand, and proficiency with a ranged weapon. Each batch produces a single projectile (arrows, bullets, bolts, or sling stones).
Heavy Ammunition. Machine gun, sniper, or bazooka ammo costs double the money.
Light Ammunition. Arrows, Bolts, and Sling bullets cost half the listed time and money.

sections.name: Special Ammunition Cost
sections.text: Legendary ammunition can only be bought at the Underworld Market in extremely low numbers or found at Marine Headquarters.

sections.name: Ammunition Types
sections.text: These rare projectiles carry unique properties. Each piece of ammunition is consumed on use.

sections.name: Element Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Uncommon
When you finish crafting this ammunition, choose one damage type other than psychic or force. On a hit, the attack deals an additional 1d6 damage of the chosen type.

sections.name: Slow Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Uncommon
On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have its movement speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

sections.name: Metallic Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Uncommon
Attacks made with this ammunition gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls. On a hit, a Medium or smaller creature must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

sections.name: Terror Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Uncommon
On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or is frightened of you until the end of its next turn.

sections.name: Tabasco Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Uncommon
On a hit, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

sections.name: Slip Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Rare
On impact, oil splashes onto all creatures within 5 feet of the target. Each creature must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. Until the oil dries (1 minute), any creature coated in oil must repeat this save at the start of its turn if it attempts to move.

sections.name: Smoke Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Rare
On impact, this shot creates a 20-foot-radius sphere of smoke centered on the point of impact. The area is heavily obscured for 1 minute, or until dispersed by moderate wind (10+ mph).

sections.name: Cactus Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Rare
On impact, the target and all creatures within 5 feet of the target take 2d4 piercing damage.

sections.name: Caltrop Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Rare
On impact, sharp caltrops scatter across a 20-foot radius centered on the target space. The area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute. When a creature moves into or through the area, it takes 2d4 piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels.

sections.name: Thunder Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Rare
On impact, all creatures within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from the point of impact.

sections.name: Dumb Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Very Rare
On a hit, the target immediately loses concentration on any spell it is maintaining.

sections.name: Poisoner Shot
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Very Rare
On a hit, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

sections.name: Seastone Bullet
sections.text:
Weapon (any ammunition), Legendary
On a hit, the target takes an additional 3d10 force damage. If the target is a Devil Fruit user, the target must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or lose access to all Devil Fruit powers until the end of its next turn, and suffer disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks during that time.

entries.name: Meitos
entries.text:
Meito are famed weapons of extraordinary quality, passed down through generations and forged by master smiths. Each is a piece of legend, often wielded by great warriors, pirates, or marines.
In this setting, the total number of named Meito is limited. Each blade carries a history, a reputation, and often a curse or legacy tied to its past owners. However, not every Meito is a named blade, many exist as Grade Meitos, which are still well made in their own regard but have not gotten to chance to make history.
If you are looking for more meitos to use in your games, check out the Dungeons and Devil Fruits Community Handbook.

sections.name: Meito Saving Throws
sections.text:
Some Meitos use the will of their user to inflict effects.
Meito save DC = 10 + half of your Willpower score

sections.name: Upgrading a Weapon into a Grade Meito
sections.text:
Any weapon, not just blades, have the potential to become a Grade Meito, but the process requires more than just coin, it also demands craftsmanship. Here are the steps to upgrading your weapon into a Grade Meito: 1. Master Smith. The weapon must be reforged or
enhanced by a smith renowned enough to handle the work.
2. Payment. The wielder must invest the required cost
in rare materials, labor, and enchantments. See the table below for upgrade cost and how many workweeks it will take the smith to enhance. If you have already enhanced a weapon you may minus the cost of your previous enhancement by the upgrades cost.
3. Meito Ability. Each time the weapon is enhanced, the
wielder of this weapon and the Dungeon Master should discuss and forge a unique ability or an upgrade to an ability for the meito to possess based around the enhancement level of the blade. All enhanced weapon are considered magical.
4. Naming the Blade. Once reforged from a mundane
item, the weapon must be given a name by its wielder. Without a name, the weapon remains a fine tool but not a true Meito. A name marks the weapon’s entry into legend and ensures its recognition as a Grade Meito.

sections.name: Skillful Grade Meitos
sections.text:
Skillful Grade Meitos are blades of exceptional craftsmanship, forged individually by master smiths and recognized by experts at a glance. While not as rare as Great or Supreme Grade weapons, the 50 that were forged are far removed from mass-produced arms.
Here are the skillful grade meitos that are known so far in the setting.

sections.name: Kashu
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿5,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A mirror-polished katana with a green silk-wrapped hilt and a minimalist guard.
Flurry of Reflections. As an action, you release a sweeping barrage of mirrored strikes in a 10 foot radius around you. Each creature of your choice within range must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes slashing damage equal to 1d8 x one quarter of your Willpower. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Mirrored Guard. When a creature you can see attacks you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll as Kashu catches and redirects the blow.
This feature can be used twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Kosho
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A sleek katana with subtle serrations along its edge, a blue silk-wrapped hilt, and a plain guard.
When you hit a creature with this weapon, the target takes an additional 1d4 slashing damage at the start of its next turn.
Serrated Arc. As an action, you sweep the blade in a massive arc. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes slashing damage equal to 1d8 x one quarter of your Willpower (rounded up) and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

sections.name: Kyokuen
sections.text:
Weapon (saber), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A fiery-red saber with a wavy, irregular arc pattern along the blade, fitted with a red silk-wrapped hilt.
Ember Reprisal. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d10 fire damage to that creature.
Ashen Wake. When you move at least 10 feet on your turn, the ground you pass over briefly smolders. The first creature that enters a space you moved through before the start of your next turn takes 1d6 fire damage.
This feature can be used twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Cursed. While attuned to this weapon, you have a −2 penalty to saving throws against being charmed or frightened. If you die while attuned to this weapon, your body is immediately reduced to ash as the saber erupts in flame, leaving behind only your equipment.

sections.name: Yamaoroshi
sections.text:
Weapon (greatsword), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
An exceptionally large katana with a thick, weighty blade and a red and black silk-wrapped hilt.
Mountain Breaker. As an action, you drive the blade into the ground with crushing force. Each creature in a 15 foot line extending from you must make a Strength saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to 1d8 x one quarter of your Willpower and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t knocked prone.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Tremor Step. When you move at least 10 feet straight toward a creature and hit it with this weapon on the same turn, the impact shakes the ground beneath it. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Meito save DC or have its speed reduced by half on its next turn.
This feature can be used twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Yubashiri
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A long katana with a black handle, a cross-shaped guard, and a black lacquered sheath.
Weightless Edge. When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can choose to immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
Afterimage Dash. When you take the Dash action, attacks of opportunity against you are made with disadvantage until the end of the turn.

sections.name: Zangetsumaru
sections.text:
Weapon (longsword), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000 You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A massive longsword etched end to end with ancient poneglyph inscriptions, fitted with a green and white silk-wrapped hilt.
When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can choose to deal an additional 1d6 force damage. The next attack roll made by another ally against that creature before the beginning of your next turn has advantage.
Cursed. While attuned to this weapon, your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22. Your Wisdom score becomes 10; if your Wisdom is already 10 or lower, it is instead reduced by 4.

sections.name: Great Grade Meitos
sections.text:
Far rarer than Skillful Grade blades, each of the 21 Great Grade Meitos is a masterpiece. These blades are typically wielded by renowned pirates, marines, or champions, and their names are spoken with reverence or fear.
Here are the great grade meitos that are known so far in the setting.

sections.name: Ame no Habakiri
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 8 or higher)
Cost: ฿500,000,000
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A moderately curved white katana with a golden trefoil tsuba, gold fittings, and matching white tsuka and saya adorned with simple five-petaled flower motifs and three binding cords.
When you hit a creature with a melee attack using this weapon, the target takes an additional 1d6 radiant damage.
Heaven-Cleaver. As an action, you release a burst of divine power in a 30 foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to 1d10 x half of your Willpower and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t blinded. You regain hit points equal to half the total damage dealt. If this healing would exceed your hit point maximum, the excess becomes temporary hit points.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Twin Blade Balance. While you are attuned to both Ame no Habakiri and Enma and wielding them in combat, you can use your action to unleash a massive cross-slash in a 30 foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes slashing damage equal to 1d10 x half of your Willpower, plus radiant and force damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Enma
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 8 or higher)
Cost: ฿500,000,000
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A moderately curved shobu zukuri katana in a lilac and gold color scheme with a ridged trefoil tsuba and a purple hilt.
When you make a melee attack with this weapon, you can choose to let Enma draw upon your Haki. If you do, inflict force damage to yourself equal 30d4 - an amount of d4s equal to your Willpower score, and the attack deals an additional 30d4 force damage. If this necrotic damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you receive 2 exhaustion point on top of any other exhaustion you would gain.
Hell-Cutter. As an action, you release Enma’s hunger in a 60 foot line. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes force damage equal to 1d10 x half of your Willpower. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage. You must then succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take half of the damage as Enma drains your life in return.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Twin Blade Balance. While you are attuned to both Ame no Habakiri and Enma and wielding them in combat, you can use your action to unleash a massive cross-slash in a 30 foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes slashing damage equal to 1d10 x half of your Willpower, plus radiant and force damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Nidai Kitetsu
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 8 or higher)
Cost: ฿500,000,000
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A moderately curved katana with a pale purple edge and a vivid blue, flame-shaped hamon running along the blade.
Drawn to Blood. When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with this weapon, you regain hit points equal to your Willpower score. While your current hit points are below half your hit point maximum, your attacks with this weapon deal an additional 1d8 slashing damage.
Crimson Thirst. As a bonus action, you awaken the blade’s inner wrath for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:
Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19–20.
When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you may teleport up to 15 feet to another creature you can see.
The first time you would drop to 0 hit points during this duration, you instead drop to 1 hit point.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.
Curse. To attune to this weapon, you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against Nidai Kitetsu’s save DC; on a failure, you take 10d6 necrotic damage and 8d6 necrotic at the end of each long rest, and if this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, your soul is absorbed into the blade permanently while it remains intact. Once attuned, you are cursed and can’t unattune from this weapon while alive. If you die while attuned, you must make a Constitution saving throw against the blade’s save DC; on a failure, your soul is absorbed.

sections.name: Shusui
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 8 or higher)
Cost: ฿500,000,000
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A jet-black katana bearing a stark reverse wave hamon in the Kanemoto style, fitted with a flower-edged octofoil tsuba.
This weapon can’t be broken by mundane means. While wielding Shusui, you have resistance to nonmagical slashing damage.
Omen of the Black Blade. At dawn, roll a d10. On a 1–2, until your next long rest your attacks with this weapon deal additional necrotic damage equal to 1d8 x half of your Willpower.
Moonlit Edge. While in dim light or darkness, your critical hits deal additional necrotic damage equal to 1d8 x one quarter of your Willpower.
Ichidai Sanzen Daisen Sekai. As an action, make a single melee attack roll against each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you. On a hit, a target takes slashing damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower plus force damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower, and must succeed on a Strength saving throw against the blade’s save DC or be pushed up to 30 feet away from you and knocked prone.
Curse. If you drop to 0 hit points while attuned, roll a d20. On a 1-3, you die and your soul is trapped within the blade, retrievable only if Shusui is destroyed. On a 4- 20, you instead return to life with 1 hit point and have advantage on attack rolls until the end of your next turn; after combat, gain all exhaustion you would normally from falling in combat, up to 5 exhaustion.

sections.name: Wado Ichimonji
sections.text:
Weapon (katana), Very Rare (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 8 or higher)
Cost: ฿500,000,000
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A pristine white katana with a pure-white silk- wrapped hilt, a circular handguard, a matching white sheath, and a straight suguha hamon running cleanly along the blade.
This weapon can’t be broken by mundane means and is immune to rust, corrosion, and magical decay. While you wield it, attempts to disarm you are made with disadvantage.
While you are below half your hit point maximum, the first attack you make with this weapon on each of your turns deals an additional 1d6 slashing damage.
Unyielding Resolve. When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to reroll the save and take the new result.
You can use this feature twice, regaining the uses when you finish a long rest.
Shishi Sonson. As an action, you dash in a straight line up to 60 feet, moving through creatures without provoking opportunity attacks. At the end of this movement, each creature whose space you passed through must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes slashing damage equal to 1d10 x half of your Willpower and is stunned until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn’t stunned.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Supreme Grade Meitos
sections.text:
Supreme Grade Meitos represent the pinnacle of craftsmanship. With only 12 are known to exist in the world, these weapons are closer to relics than arms.
Here are the supreme grade meitos that are known so far in the setting.

sections.name: Ace
sections.text:
Weapon (cutlass), Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A normal-sized cutlass with a slightly curved blade bearing a saw-shaped hamon, a yellow diamond- patterned hilt, a golden dome-shaped guard, and a thin knuckle guard running along the grip.
While attuned to this weapon, you have resistance to lightning and force damage.
While Ace is visibly carried on your person, you have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) and Charisma (Persuasion) checks. When you fail one of these checks, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this property, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.
Blade of the King. As an action, you awaken the immense Haki sealed within Ace. Until you use a bonus action to end this effect, or until you drop or sheathe the weapon, your weapon attacks made by Ace deal an additional 2d8 lightning damage and 2d8 force damage on a hit.
Conqueror’s Wake. When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with Ace or score a critical hit, choose one creature of your choice within 30 feet that can see you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Meito save DC or be frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
Divine Departure. As part of the Attack action, you can empower a strike with overwhelming force. On a hit, the attack deals additional force damage equal to 2d10 x half of your Willpower, and the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 60 feet away from you.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Murakumogiri
sections.text:
Weapon (glaive), Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A massive tomoe-style naginata with a red-and-yellow striped pole ending in a spherical pommel, bearing a huge curved blade secured by a brass bolster engraved with a sea serpent and reinforced by langets running onto the steel.
While you are wielding Murakumogiri, you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked prone, or forcibly moved.
When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit a creature with Murakumogiri, you can immediately make one additional melee weapon attack against a different creature within 10 feet of your reach.
Heaven-Splitting Swing. When you hit a creature with a melee attack using this weapon, you can unleash a cataclysmic swing. The attack deals additional magical slashing damage equal to 1d10 x one quarter of your Willpower, and each creature of your choice within 15 feet of the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Meito save DC or be pushed 20 feet away and knocked prone.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Quake. As an action, you can drive Murakumogiri into the ground, releasing a devastating shockwave in a 30 foot radius. Each other creature in the area must make a Strength saving throw against your Meito save DC, taking force damage equal to 2d10 x half of your Willpower and falling prone on a failed save, or half as much damage without falling prone on a success. Structures and objects in the area automatically take double damage from this effect.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Shodai Kitetsu
sections.text:
Weapon (longsword), Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A long tachi-style blade of nodachi length with a flame-shaped hamon, a pale-gold four-lobed tsuba, and a wooden-finished saya characteristic of the Kitetsu line.
This weapon can’t be broken by mundane means. While wielding Shodai Kitetsu, your reach with it increases by 5 feet, and your attacks ignore resistance and immunities to magical and non-magical slashing damage.
Adaptive Length. Shodai Kitetsu grows proportionally with your size. For every token size above medium, the weapon’s reach and the length of its line based effects increase by an additional 10 feet.
Heaven Cleaving. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with this blade, you may target a creature or object up to 60 feet away.
World-Splitting Stroke. As an action, you unleash a single flawless slash. Each creature and object in a 120 foot long, 10 foot wide line originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC, taking slashing damage equal to 2d12 x half of your Willpower on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.
Curse. Once attuned, you can’t willingly unattune from this weapon. When you roll a natural 1 on an attack roll with Shodai Kitetsu, the next attack roll made against you before the end of your next turn has advantage.

sections.name: Yakuza Kasen
sections.text:
Weapon (cane sword) Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
A plain wooden walking cane concealing a straight, guardless blade, indistinguishable from an ordinary staff until drawn.
While attuned to this weapon, you gain tremorsense out to 60 feet, you ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble, uneven ground, or debris, and you have advantage on Dexterity saving throws made to avoid being knocked prone.
Visionary’s Quickguard. When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d12 x your Willpower. If this reduces the damage to 0, you may immediately make one melee weapon attack with Yakuza Kasen against the attacker or another creature within range as part of the same reaction.
Gravity Blade. As an action, you partially draw the blade, unleashing a crushing gravitational pulse in a 30 foot radius sphere centered on you. Each creature of your choice in the area when you first use this feature or at the start of your turns must make a Strength saving throw against your Meito Save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes force damage equal to 2d8 x half of your Willpower and is either knocked prone. On a success, it takes half damage and doesnt get knocked prone. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

sections.name: Yoru
sections.text:
Weapon (greatsword), Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
An enormous, cross-shaped greatsword with a curved, single-edged black blade, fashioned in a western kriegsmesser style and towering well over two meters in length.
While wielding Yoru, you gain advantage on opportunity attacks, and your opportunity attacks with Yoru reduce the target’s speed to 0 until the end of the current turn on a hit.
Kokuto Saku. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack with Yoru against the attacker. On a hit, the target takes Yoru’s normal weapon damage plus force damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower.
Kokuto Kogetsu. As an action, make a number of melee weapon attacks equal to your proficiency bonus against creatures or objects you can see within a 30 foot radius sphere centered on you. On each hit, the attack deals force damage equal to 1d6 x one quarter of your Willpower instead of the weapon’s normal damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.
Kokuto Issen. As an action, release a supreme slash in a 120 foot long, 5 foot wide line originating from you. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC, taking force damage equal to 1d12 x one half of your Willpower on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Nonmagical, non- seastone, and non-haki-infused objects and structures in the line are cleaved apart.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Additional Weapons
entries.text: This section is for any weapons that are in the show but don’t count as a Meito.

sections.name: Bamboo
sections.text:
Weapon (longsword), Uncommon (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿5,000,000 You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
This perfectly straight blade boasts a green-and- yellow hilt, a straight-edged tsuba, and a trapezoidal pommel with a cross engraving.
Attacks with Bamboo deal double damage to objects, ships, and large structures. In addition, when you hit a creature that is at least one size larger than you or an object or structure, the attack deals an extra 3d4 slashing damage.

sections.name: Cat Claws
sections.text:
Weapon (brass knuckles), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with unarmed attacks on top of the +2 bonus to damage rolls with unarmed attack.
These black furred gloves bear katana-like blades at each fingertip. Your unarmed attack damage is slashing when wearing these gloves.
Shakushi. As an action, you unleash a storm of claw strikes in a 10 feet radius around you. Each creature must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC. On a failure a creature takes 2d6 slashing damage. On a success, they take half as much damage. You can use this ability an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

sections.name: Daisenso
sections.text:
Weapon (spear), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
This massive spear extends to strike distant foes and detonates with explosives.
Explosive Impetus. When you hit a creature with Daisenso, you may cause an explosion. The target takes an additional 2d6 fire damage, and each creature within 5 feet of the target other than yourself must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Meito save DC or take 2d6 fire damage. On a success, they take half as much damage. You can use this ability an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short rest.

sections.name: Durandal
sections.text:
Weapon (rapier), Rare (requires attunement)
Cost: ฿25,000,000
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
Durandals sheath and hilt have a dark-light colored, vertical-striped pattern. The hilt adorned with several rings and graven flowers.
Elegant Riposte. When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to immediately make one melee attack with Durandal against that creature.

sections.name: Gryphon
sections.text:
Weapon (saber), Legendary (requires attunement by a creature with a willpower of 14 or higher)
Cost: ฿1,000,000,000
You have a +4 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Underworld Marketplace THE UNDERWORLD IS A SPRAWLING NETWORK OF
smugglers, brokers, and crime lords who traffic in goods too rare for ordinary markets. Its
operations thrive across the Grand Line, with secretive auctions and black markets drawing pirates, nobles, and powerful figures seeking items that the World Government would never allow to circulate openly.
Some underworld markets hide in plain sight, disguised as lavish trade houses or exclusive clubs for the wealthy. Others lurk in the shadows of remote ports, accessible only by those with the right contacts. What all share in common is the promise of rarity: treasures and tools that can change the tide of battle or fortune.

entries.name: Slavery in the Setting
entries.text:
The practice of slavery is an infamous reality in the world of One Piece, perpetuated by the world’s authorities and the darkest corners of the Underworld. Non-human races such as Fish-men, Giants, and Merfolk are frequent victims of this cruelty. While slavery remains a major theme within the setting, it is not represented mechanically in this system. Instead, DMs may choose to acknowledge or exclude its presence in their campaigns according to their table’s comfort level.
Devil Fruits. The most coveted treasures on the underwolrd market, Devil Fruits grant supernatural powers at the cost of the sea’s fury. Their exact abilities are rarely known until consumed.
Dials. Imported from the Sky Islands, Dials are shells capable of storing and releasing energy.
Meitos. Renowned named blades, or Meito, are among the most prestigious underworld market items. Each blade carries a unique power for dedicated swordsmen to unlock. Some meitos are cursed, sold at discounted prices to lure reckless buyers into buying them.
Other Magic Items. The underworld market occasionally trades in other powerful artifacts and equipment outside of typical weapons and armors.
Eternal Poses. Eternal Poses are specialized compasses that permanently point to a single island making them priceless navigational tools for any crew looking to cross the grand line.
Devil Fruit Appraisal. Specialists within the underworld market offer Devil Fruit appraisal services to learn more about a Devil Fruit you may possess.
Rare Materials. From Adam Wood to exotic metals and monster hides, the underworld market supplies rare crafting materials in bulk.
Seastone Bullets. Among the deadliest contraband, Seastone Bullets suppress Devil Fruit powers on impact.
